newsitem.title: THAILAND: Merger seen sparking Thai finance sector upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Merger seen sparking Thai finance sector upgrade.

text.p: The merger of Finance One Plc, Thailand's largest finance firm, with medium-sized Thai Danu Bank is a harbinger of further consolidation in the troubled Thai finance sector, analysts said on Sunday.

News over the weekend of the merger was welcomed by analysts, who said a further shakeout in the industry could strengthen other finance firms hit by liquidity crunches and poor-quality loans to the ailing property sector.

"This marks the first step in a process of accelerated financial reform. There will be lots more mergers, acquisitions and probably collapses. We are going to go through a painful consolidation phase that is long overdue," Graham Caterwell, country manager for Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, told Reuters.
"It's better if there are fewer numbers but stronger financial institutions," he said.
A central bank official told Reuters on Friday that some weaker finance companies had sought help from the central bank's Financial Institutions Development Fund.
Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond said he backed the planned merger.

"I personally agree with the move which is basically a normal commercial merger designed for strengthening their business and efficiency as well as trimming their expenses," he told reporters on Saturday.
Somchai Phagapasvivat, an economics professor at Thammasat University said: "This has come about because financial institutions are in the process of changing their strategies and structures now."
Officials of the two firms were unavailable for comment.
Thai Danu Bank is the 12th largest bank in the country with assets of 120 billion baht ($4.6 billion). Finance One already has a five percent stake in the bank.

Details of the proposed merger, the biggest shake-up in the domestic financial sector in more than a decade, would likely be announced on Monday and take time to be completed, finance ministry sources said at the weekend.
The merger would be subject to the approval of shareholders and Thai regulatory authorities and could result in the integration of Finance One into Thai Danu Bank, they said.

Finance One, with assets of more than 100 billion baht ($3.8 billion), was the target of rumours this week that it faced a run on deposits from major clients and has had to pay high premiums to secure funds. It denied the rumours on Friday.
"The merger is a confirmation that Finance One may have some financial problems," Kasem Prunratanamala, banking analyst at James Capel Asia, said on Saturday.
"Investors will now begin to question the stability and health of other finance firms after this news," he said.

Other analysts said the news of the merger was somewhat surprising because the two had last year sought to integrate. At that time Finance One had wanted to take over Thai Danu Bank but regulatory authorities turned down its request.
"The predator has now become the prey. I see this more as a Thai Danu takeover of Finance One than as the reverse," said another analyst who declined to be identified.
Finance One is also a major shareholder in another leading securities firm, Securities One Plc. One Holdings Plc is its investment arm.
